recommendation: Keep the source fix. issue_request: FHIR-50391 was an Applied FHIR-core R6 change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking for clearer rules around constraints, mustSupport, and obligations on repeated and sliced elements, including ElementDefinition slicing guidance, Implementation Obligations guidance, a profiling-page cross-reference, and publisher/tooling hints.
initial_application: Upstream commit 3f3077a286d669ed69f2cb51540b8f3aef58a433 applied most of the core narrative work by adding the ElementDefinition slicing list, the obligations.html repeating-element mustSupport paragraph, and a corrected child-element Must Support sentence in profiling.html. It did not add the requested profiling-page sentence directing readers to the Implementation Obligations page and it left the older duplicate child-element paragraph with the typo 'if it support the parent'. No prior Issue-Reconcile-Key commit for FHIR-50391 existed on the combined branch.
additional_context: FHIR-50390 is the companion Published FHIR Extension Pack issue that added the applicable-number obligation component referenced by the FHIR-50391 slicing guidance; the extension-pack checkout contains that component and its slicing comment. FHIR-I minutes from 2025-07-14 record the 6-0-1 approval of FHIR-50391, and the linked Zulip thread records the ambiguity around slicers, bindings, mustSupport, obligations, and applicable-number that motivated the clarification. source/hierarchy.xml includes elementdefinition.html, profiling.html, and obligations.html, confirming the edited narrative page is in current build scope.
reconciliation: Changed source/profiling.html to add the missing sentence pointing implementers to the Implementation Obligations page for mustSupport and obligations on elements with max cardinality greater than one and slices of repeating elements. Removed the directly related duplicate legacy child-element Must Support paragraph, leaving the corrected version from the upstream application as the single statement of that rule.
